podcast.title: Best New Solo Artist Juno Award (1998)
podcast.body: Holly McNeil won the Juno Award for Best New Solo Artist in 1998, recognizing her emergence as a significant talent. "This is the best new solo artist winner at the June Awards in 1998."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Additional Vocal Contributions
podcast.body: Her name can be found in the liner notes of albums by artists like Matt Good and The Tea Party, where she provided additional vocals. "But if you look at the liner notes by some albums by Matt Good and the Tea Party, you'll see that her name appears there when it comes to additional vocals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Context of Female Singers Era
podcast.body: Her career coincided with an era characterized by a wave of angry and empowered young female singers, placing her alongside artists like Alanis Morissette, Shirley Manson, Fiona Apple, Meredith Brooks, and Courtney Love. "That was an era of angry, empowered young female singers. Think Alannas Morseh. There was Shirley Manson, Fiona Apple, Meredith Brooks, Courtney Love, and Holly was part of all that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Performance for Charitable Causes
podcast.body: Holly McNeil is still frequently called upon to perform, particularly for benefit events supporting Aboriginal causes, Métis events, and MS research. "Holly is still called on to perform. She has a lot of benefits stuff. Aboriginal causes, May T events, benefits for MS research. That sort of thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Instagram Profile Details
podcast.body: Her Instagram profile offers a glimpse into her current life, listing her roles as a parent and singer-songwriter, as well as her interests in food, interior design, and maintaining an income property. "And her Instagram profile lists her as a parent and singer-songwriter, and as someone who is into food, interior design, and maintaining an income property."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Métis Heritage and Aboriginal Involvement
podcast.body: Holly McNeil is Métis and hails from The Pas in Northern Manitoba, and she has actively engaged in various Aboriginal projects throughout her career. "Holly is May T and is originally from the Pah in Northern Manitoba. She became involved in a number of Aboriginal projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Parenthood
podcast.body: She became a parent, which became another focus in her life alongside her musical pursuits. "and she also became a parent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
